hello.note: More formal: selamat sejahtera. Between Muslims: assalamualaikum (reply: waalaikumussalam).

goodbye.note: Said by the one leaving. The one staying behind says selamat jalan.

please.note: Asks someone to do something. Sila invites them: sila duduk (please sit). To ask for a thing: minta …

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: terima kasih banyak.

no.note: Casual: tak. To say 'not' before a noun or pronoun, use bukan: bukan saya (not me).

excuse_me.note: Used before asking a stranger something. To get past someone: tumpang lalu.

how_are_you.note: Also works as a general greeting, like hello.

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: siapa nama cik? (puan if she is older or married). Anda works for anyone but sounds formal.

where_from.note: To a woman: cik (or puan) berasal dari mana? Casual: asal dari mana?

speak_english.note: Politer with a title first: encik boleh cakap … (cik to a woman).

speak_slowly.note: Sikit is the everyday form of sedikit (a little).

where.note: Casual: kat mana? or just mana?

what.note: Apa dia? sounds softer when you didn't catch what was said.

where_bathroom.note: Bilik air (washroom) is also common. Casual: tandas kat mana?

what_time.note: Answer with pukul + number: pukul tiga (three o'clock).

one.note: Before a counter word it becomes se-: seorang (one person), sebuah (one thing).

eight.note: Indonesian says delapan; in Malaysia it is lapan.

ten.note: Eleven is sebelas, twenty is dua puluh.

water.note: Order plain water as air kosong, or ais kosong for iced water. Pronounced ah-eer.

coffee.note: Kopi comes with condensed milk; kopi O is black with sugar.

tea.note: Teh tarik is frothy 'pulled' milk tea; teh O is without milk.

bill_please.note: At a casual stall people often just say kira! (add it up).

no_meat.note: Daging often means red meat only; add ayam pun tak (no chicken either) to be clear.

enjoy_meal.note: A host inviting you to start: jemput makan.

airport.note: In everyday speech many people simply say airport.

hotel.note: Same word as in English, said ho-tel with even stress.

train_station.note: Kereta alone means car. For city rail: stesen LRT or stesen MRT.

want_to_go.note: In everyday speech: saya nak pergi ke …

one_ticket.note: With a destination: minta satu tiket ke …

cheaper.note: To bargain: boleh kurang sikit? (can you lower it a bit?)

id_like_this.note: Also saya ambil yang ini (I'll take this one).

cash.note: To pay in cash: bayar tunai. Many people just say cash.

yesterday.note: Semalam can also mean last night.

good_evening.note: Used from mid-afternoon until dusk. After dark, greet with selamat malam.

good_night.note: Also a greeting after dark. Right before bed: selamat tidur.

see_you_later.note: If you'll meet again the same day: jumpa nanti.

call_police.note: The emergency number in Malaysia is 999.

need_doctor.note: Also saya perlu jumpa doktor (I need to see a doctor).

dont_feel_well.note: Kurang sihat is the polite, usual way to say it. Casual: tak sihat.

hospital.note: Same word as in English. For minor problems, look for a klinik.

allergic.note: Example: saya alah kepada kacang (nuts). Many people also say saya alergik …

be_careful.note: Also jaga-jaga! Warning signs say awas.

no_problem.note: Tak apa (it's fine, never mind) is also very common.

maybe.note: Casual speech often adds kot at the end of a sentence instead.

my_family.note: Possessives follow the noun: ibu saya (my mother), kawan saya (my friend).

mother.note: Children usually say mak or emak. Parents: ibu bapa.

father.note: Children usually say ayah or abah.

brother.note: An older brother; a younger one is adik lelaki. Abang is also a friendly way to address a man.

sister.note: An older sister; a younger one is adik perempuan. Kak is also a friendly way to address a woman.

child.note: Son: anak lelaki; daughter: anak perempuan. Children in general: kanak-kanak.

friend.note: Same for a man or a woman. Also rakan (more formal) or sahabat (a close friend).

this_is_my_friend.note: Same for a male or female friend.

are_you_married.note: To a woman: cik sudah berkahwin? Casual: dah kahwin?

have_children.note: To a woman: puan ada anak? A polite 'no' is belum lagi (not yet).

monday.note: Day names usually follow hari: hari Isnin. On Monday: pada hari Isnin.

friday.note: Many offices take a long lunch break on Friday for midday prayers.

sunday.note: Also hari Minggu, the usual word in Indonesia.

weekend.note: In a few states, such as Kelantan, the weekend is Friday and Saturday.

eleven.note: The teens use belas: dua belas (12), tiga belas (13) and so on.

twenty.note: Tens use puluh. Twenty-one: dua puluh satu.

hundred.note: Se- means one: seratus (100), but dua ratus (200).

thousand.note: Two thousand: dua ribu. A million: sejuta.

how_old.note: To a woman: berapa umur cik? (puan if she is older or married).

red.note: Colours follow the noun: baju merah (a red shirt).

blue.note: Dark blue: biru tua; light blue: biru muda.

what_colour.note: Casual: warna apa ni? (what colour is this?)

another_one.note: With an item: teh tarik satu lagi (another teh tarik).

its_hot.note: The -nya makes it an exclamation, like 'so hot!'. Plainly: cuaca panas.

its_raining.note: Casual: tengah hujan. Heavy rain: hujan lebat.

its_sunny.note: Cerah means clear and bright. Blazing sun: panas terik.

weather_today.note: Casual: cuaca hari ni macam mana?

beautiful_day.note: Cantik (pretty) is often used for nice weather. Plainer: cuaca baik hari ini.

summer.note: Malaysia is hot all year; its seasons are musim hujan (rainy) and musim kemarau (dry).

winter.note: Literally 'cold season'. Indonesian says musim dingin.

have_reservation.note: Many people simply say booking: saya ada booking.

room.note: Bilik air is a bathroom, bilik tidur a bedroom.

luggage.note: Everyday: beg (bags), as in beg saya (my bags).

wifi_password.note: Most people just say password: password Wi-Fi apa?

check_out_time.note: Most people just say check-out: check-out pukul berapa?

bus.note: Bus stop: perhentian bas. Bus station: stesen bas.

next_train.note: For LRT or MRT people say tren: tren seterusnya pukul berapa?

is_this_seat_free.note: Also common: ada orang duduk sini? (is anyone sitting here?)

what_do_you_do.note: To a woman: cik (or puan) bekerja sebagai apa? Casual: kerja apa?

i_work_in.note: Di is for a place: di bank. For a field: dalam bidang …, e.g. dalam bidang jualan (sales).

im_student.note: Same for a man or a woman. At university: pelajar universiti.

meeting.note: In everyday office talk many people say meeting.

im_busy.note: Busy right now: saya tengah sibuk.

day_off.note: Cuti means leave or a holiday: saya cuti hari ini (I'm off today).

colleague.note: Same for a man or a woman. Casual: kawan sekerja or kawan ofis.

table_for_two.note: Staff often ask berapa orang? (how many?): just answer dua orang.

what_recommend.note: Literally 'what's tasty here?' More formal: apa yang encik cadangkan?

not_spicy.note: Just a little less spicy: kurang pedas.

vegetarian_food.note: I'm vegetarian: saya vegetarian, or saya makan sayur sahaja.

more_water.note: Also tambah air, ya (top up the water).

no_sugar.note: Less sweet: kurang manis. Kosong after a drink means no sugar: teh O kosong.

takeaway.note: Very common slang: tapau. Eating in: makan sini.

it_was_delicious.note: Malay has no past tense, so this covers 'was'. Casual: sedap betul!

keep_change.note: Casual: tak payah baki. Tipping isn't expected in Malaysia.

head_hurts.note: Same pattern: sakit perut (stomachache), sakit tekak (sore throat).

have_fever.note: No verb needed: demam means having a fever. A cold is selsema.

medicine.note: Taking medicine is makan ubat, literally 'eating' it.

dentist.note: Gigi means teeth; a toothache is sakit gigi.

need_rest.note: Casual: saya kena rehat (I have to rest). Also common: nak rehat kejap (I want a short rest).

feel_better.note: Casual: dah okey sikit (a bit better now).

are_you_free.note: To a woman: cik lapang esok? Many people say free: esok free tak?

call_me.note: Many people just say call: nanti call saya.

your_number.note: To a woman: berapa nombor telefon cik? Malay asks for numbers with berapa.

see_you_soon.note: Shorter: jumpa lagi. Sampai jumpa lagi is also heard, mostly on TV and radio.

have_nice_day.note: Less set than in English. Shop staff more often say terima kasih, datang lagi! (come again).

miss_you.note: Between close friends: aku rindu kau. To family, use their title: rindu mak (I miss you, Mum).
